correctness.rationale: Reconstructed each conditional expectation as a four-state row/column weighted averaging matrix, multiplied their products, and derived the commutator with entries expressed in four conditional probabilities. The two cross-conditional gaps have the sign of ad-bc, so each absolute row sum reduces to twice the larger of two nonnegative coefficients. The fixed-odds bound follows by optimizing the Bernoulli difference |theta-1|t/((1+t)(1+theta t)) over all t>0. A full-support explicit family with fixed theta converges to equality, whereas every individual positive table is strict when theta!=1. A standalone rational independent matrix checker passed all 4096 positive integer quadruples of masses 1..8 and 15 sharp-sequence checks. The unrestricted claim is established by algebra, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: The order of two conditional reconstructions affects output observables, yet the classical binary odds ratio only measures scalar association. This theorem gives an exact computable per-table operator error and a best-possible margin-free quantitative bound whose limiting extremizers are classified constructively. Distinguishing strict positivity and nonattainment is essential: the largest order defect under fixed association is only approached by extreme marginal imbalance. The sharp analysis has a motivated stability application and is not just a restatement of Yule Y.
